title: Places to Visit Near Jaipur Under 150 km: Day Trips
summary: Best places to visit near Jaipur under 150 km covering Pushkar, Ajmer, Sariska, Sambhar Lake, Alwar, Neemrana and Chand Baori.
body_markdown:
A 150 km radius from Jaipur contains a surprising range. Sufi shrines, a tiger reserve, India’s largest salt lake, one of the deepest stepwells in the country, a Mughal-era fort turned luxury hotel, and the only Brahma temple in active worship. All of these sit within a morning’s drive from the Pink City.


The list below covers destinations that genuinely fall within the 150 km threshold, with actual driving distances rather than rounded estimates. Each one is a realistic day trip or a comfortable overnight trip from Jaipur.


# **Places to Visit Near Jaipur Under 150 km: A Practical Travel Guide**


The destinations are arranged by distance band rather than alphabetical order. Closer options come first, which makes planning easier when you have limited time.


## **Under 50 km: The Closest Escapes**


### **Sanganer, about 16 km**


Sanganer is where Jaipur’s famous block-printed textiles are actually made. The workshops here produce the hand-stamped cotton and silk that gets sold under the Jaipur label in stores across the country. The Sanganer Jain Temple, built in the 10th century, carries intricate carved panels across its exterior.


### **Bagru, about 32 km**


Bagru is the older of Jaipur’s two printing villages and produces the distinctive indigo and red Bagru prints using mud-resist techniques that have survived for over 300 years. The village is less commercial than Sanganer and gives a clearer look at the actual dyeing process.


### **Samode, about 42 km**


Samode Palace, a 475-year-old fortified palace in the foothills of the Aravallis, is still operational as a heritage hotel. The Sheesh Mahal inside the palace, entirely covered in mirror work, is one of the more striking interiors in Rajasthan.


## **50 to 100 km: Half-Day Territory**


### **Sambhar Lake, about 82 km**


Sambhar is India’s largest inland salt lake, stretching over 230 square kilometres. The Sambhar Salt works here have been operating since at least the 6th century. Between November and February, the lake becomes a wintering ground for flamingos, with populations that have historically crossed 100,000 birds in good years.


### **Bhangarh Fort, about 84 km**


Bhangarh is officially listed by the Archaeological Survey of India, and a notice at the entrance prohibits entry between sunset and sunrise. The fort complex covers an entire abandoned town, with temples, markets, havelis and a royal palace spread across the site. The construction dates to 1573 under Raja Bhagwant Das.


### **Chand Baori, Abhaneri, about 95 km**


Chand Baori is a stepwell built in the 8th century under King Chanda of the Nikumbha dynasty. It descends 13 stories and contains approximately 3,500 narrow steps arranged in a geometric pattern. At about 20 metres deep, it is one of the deepest and largest stepwells in India. The Harshat Mata Temple stands directly adjacent.


## **100 to 150 km: Full Day Trips and Overnights**


### **Sariska Tiger Reserve, about 107 km**


Sariska sits in the Aravalli hills and covers about 866 square kilometres. It was India’s first tiger reserve to receive relocated tigers, with the first animals moved here from Ranthambore in 2008 after Sariska’s entire tiger population was lost to poaching by 2004. The park is open from October to June, with the best sighting window between March and June when the vegetation thins and tigers come to waterholes.


### **Neemrana Fort Palace, about 122 km**


Neemrana Fort dates to 1464 and has been converted into a heritage hotel that spreads across 14 levels on the hillside. The zip line across the fort ramparts is one of the longer ones in Rajasthan. For travellers headed towards or from Delhi, Neemrana works as a midpoint stop.


### **Ajmer, about 135 km**


Ajmer Sharif Dargah, the shrine of Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, dates to the 13th century and draws visitors across religious lines throughout the year. The Urs festival, held annually in the Islamic month of Rajab, is the largest gathering. Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra, a partially ruined mosque about 500 metres from the Dargah, was originally a Sanskrit college before its conversion in 1199 CE. Ana Sagar Lake, built by Anaji Chauhan in the 12th century, sits on the city’s northern edge.


### **Pushkar, about 145 km**


Pushkar sits on the other side of the Nag Pahar hill from Ajmer, connected by a road that crosses a narrow pass. The Brahma Temple here is among the very few temples in the world dedicated to Brahma. Pushkar Lake is surrounded by 52 ghats, and the town sees its peak activity during the Pushkar Camel Fair, held annually in November around Kartik Purnima.


### **Alwar, about 150 km**


Alwar is one of Rajasthan’s oldest cities and the gateway to Sariska. The Bala Quila fort sits above the city and dates to the 15th century, though parts of the structure are believed to be older. Siliserh Lake, about 13 km from the city centre, is a quiet water body with a former hunting lodge on its banks.


## **How to Plan These Trips From Jaipur**


The under-50 km destinations work as morning excursions without an overnight stay. Sambhar, Bhangarh and Chand Baori are all feasible as single-day round trips leaving early and returning by evening.


Sariska, Ajmer, Pushkar, Neemrana and Alwar benefit from an overnight stay, particularly if the visit is over a weekend. Ajmer and Pushkar are close enough to combine into a single two-day trip.


For bus connections from Jaipur, check current schedules and options on the[Jaipur bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/jaipur-bus-booking-online) . The Jaipur to Ajmer corridor is among the busier intercity routes in Rajasthan.


## **Best Time to Visit**


October through March is the practical travel season for the places to visit near jaipur under 150 km. Daytime temperatures in this window range from the mid-teens to the high twenties, making outdoor sightseeing and fort visits comfortable.


Sambhar Lake’s flamingo season runs from November to February. Sariska is best between March and June for wildlife sightings. Pushkar Camel Fair falls in November. The summer months from April to June push temperatures above 40 degrees across this region and are best avoided for outdoor exploration.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Which places near Jaipur are best for a day trip under 150 km?**


Sambhar Lake, Bhangarh Fort, Chand Baori and Sariska Tiger Reserve are all realistic day trips within the 150 km radius.


### **How far is Pushkar from Jaipur?**


Pushkar is about 145 km from Jaipur, roughly a three-hour drive through Ajmer on NH48.


### **Is Sariska Tiger Reserve open year round?**


Sariska is open from October to June and closes during the monsoon months from July to September.


### **What is special about Chand Baori near Jaipur?**


Chand Baori is an 8th century stepwell with approximately 3,500 steps descending 13 stories, making it one of the deepest in India.


### **Can I visit Ajmer and Pushkar on the same trip from Jaipur?**


Yes, Ajmer and Pushkar are about 14 km apart and combine naturally into a single day trip or overnight from Jaipur.


### **What is the best time to visit places near jaipur under 150 km?**


October through March offers comfortable temperatures and the best conditions for outdoor sightseeing across this region.


### **Is there a bus from Jaipur to Ajmer or Pushkar?**


Multiple daily bus services connect Jaipur to Ajmer, and Pushkar is reachable from Ajmer by local transport.


### **What should I see at Bhangarh Fort?**


The fort complex includes a full abandoned town with temples, a royal palace and market ruins dating to 1573.


### **Is Sambhar Lake worth visiting in winter?**


November to February is the best window for Sambhar, when flamingo populations gather and the lake’s surface reflects the sky.


### **How far is Neemrana Fort from Jaipur?**


Neemrana Fort Palace is about 122 km from Jaipur, roughly two hours on NH48 towards Delhi.
